title: [TTTv2] Four pre-existing defects in models/common surfaced by the tier-1 CI migration: attention decode PCC, Sampling1DConfig.local_indices, rmsnorm tolerance, load_tensor SIGBUS
body:
## Summary

Migrating the TTTv2 module suites into the tiered Models CI pipelines (#53911) ran them under conditions the T3K pipelines never applied — a forced watcher, a read-only `/mnt/MLPerf`, and a cold tensor cache. That surfaced four distinct pre-existing defects in `models/common`, plus one infrastructure gap. None is caused by the migration; all are reproducible on `main`.

This issue collects them so they can be split into per-owner fixes. Two of them currently make the TT-Transformers tier-1 unit gate red on landing.

Evidence throughout is from run [32516753713](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/actions/runs/32516753713) on `wh_llmbox`, with `/mnt/MLPerf` mounted read-write and no watcher, against a `tt_cache/tttv2/attention_1d` regenerated from empty. Results were byte-identical to run [32510125078](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/actions/runs/32510125078), so these are deterministic, not flakes.

Per-module results in that run:

| Module | Result |
|---|---|
| `models/common/tests` (non-module) | 1 failed / 1718 passed / 248 skipped |
| mlp | 28 passed |
| rmsnorm | 27 passed |
| rope | 42 passed |
| lm_head | 13 passed |
| **attention** | **16 failed** / 24 passed / 14 skipped |
| embedding | 19 passed |
| penalties | 81 passed |
| **sampling** | **71 failed** / 53 passed |

---

## A · `Sampling1DConfig` is missing `local_indices` — 71 failures

`models/common/modules/sampling/sampling_1d.py:194`, in `load_device_buffers()`:

```python
self._local_indices = _materialize(cfg.local_indices)
```

`Sampling1DConfig` (same file, lines 53-90) does not declare that field, so this raises:

```
AttributeError: 'Sampling1DConfig' object has no attribute 'local_indices'
```

`release()` reads the same name via `getattr(self.config, name, None)`, so only the load path dies.

**This is a half-applied revert, not a missing field.** #53001 (`b915f58d5f0`, 08-17) removed the iota `local_indices` buffer wholesale — it was the subject of #52928, where `ttnn.topk` received an `indices_tensor` half the width of the logits and returned indices that did not match the values beside them. #51184 (`310f9ef60fa`, 08-19) rewrote `load_device_buffers()` to add `try`/`release()` handling and carried the deleted reader back with it.

State on `main`:

| Piece | State |
|---|---|
| `Sampling1DConfig.local_indices` field | deleted by #53001 |
| its builder (`_make_local_indices`, `to_set["local_indices"]`) | deleted by #53001 |
| `required_buffers` (line 105) | correct — no `local_indices` |
| reader `cfg.local_indices` (line 194) | resurrected → `AttributeError` |
| `_topk_single_device` slice + `ttnn.split` (574-577) | resurrected; the resulting `indices_list` is never used |
| `_topk_multi_device` slice + `indices_tensor=local_indices` (619-627) | resurrected |

**Re-adding the field is the wrong direction** — it reinstates the buffer #53001 deliberately dropped, and the builder is gone anyway. The fix is to finish that removal: drop the line 194 reader, the dead slice/split in `_topk_single_device`, and the slice plus `indices_tensor=` argument in `_topk_multi_device`, letting `ttnn.topk` generate the index tile itself. #53001 verified that bit-identical to the iota buffer at twelve widths, across both program factories and the UINT16→UINT32 boundary. Four deletions, roughly a dozen lines, nothing added.

One caveat: #53001 only ever fixed the single-device path — its own notes record 1×2 measuring zero mismatches and 1×8 / 4×8 unmeasured — so dropping `indices_tensor=` on the multi-device path is new ground and wants a run behind it.

---

## B · Attention decode-path PCC failures — 16 failures

`models/common/tests/modules/attention/test_attention_1d.py`, PCC as low as **0.1498**:

```
FAILED test_attention_1d_vs_reference[10-standard-1x{1,2,8}-decode-32-{1B,8B0,11B}-…]
FAILED test_attention_1d_vs_reference[10-paged-1x{1,2,8}-decode-32-{1B,8B0,11B}-…]
FAILED test_attention_1d_prefill_decode_transition[{paged,non-paged}-1x{1,2,8}]
FAILED test_attention_prefill_selects_scalar_or_tensor_chunk_start_api[{True,False}]
```

Observed PCC values span 0.1498 – 0.66 against passing cases at 1.0.

Notable characteristics:

- **Every failure is on the decode path** (`-decode-32-`) or the prefill→decode transition. Prefill-only cases pass.
- Affects **1×1, 1×2 and 1×8** alike, so not mesh- or CCL-specific.
- Affects **Llama 1B, 8B and 11B** — models *without* Q/K bias. `models/common/tests/modules/attention/low_pcc_notes.md` documents a HuggingFace-vs-Meta RoPE permutation of the Q/K **bias** as a known degradation source, but that mechanism requires a bias and does not apply here. So this is not the documented case.
- **Not cache-related.** Reproduced identically against a `tt_cache/tttv2/attention_1d` deleted and regenerated from empty, with the mount read-write so nothing fell back.
- **Not watcher-related.** No watcher active; zero watcher events in the log.
- Deterministic: identical counts and 3:57 duration across two independent runs.

This one I could not attribute to a specific commit and I do not believe it is tracked elsewhere. It is the highest-value item here — a decode-path PCC of 0.15 means wrong output, not marginal drift.

---

## C · `test_validation_rmsnorm_host_and_device[1x1]` tolerance failure — 1 failure

```
max_abs_error=3.125000e-02 exceeds tolerance 1.000000e-02
```

`models/common/tests/test_validation_tools.py`. Pre-existing on `main` — the same single failure appears in the `t3k_tttv2_fast_unit_tests` job on `main` ([run 32489962502](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/actions/runs/32489962502)). Either a real regression or a tolerance that needs revisiting; it is the only failure in the 1719-case non-module suite.

---

## D · `all_gather_async` assert — already tracked

Running the attention suite under `TT_METAL_WATCHER=30` reproduces **G1 of #50886** / #49081: exit 134, watcher assert in the `minimal_default_reader` NCRISC kernel, fabric EDM router hang, on the 8-chip mesh. Recorded on both issues already; noted here only for completeness. It is invisible with the watcher off, which is how the migrated entries now run.

---

## E · Infrastructure: `ttnn.load_tensor` raises `SIGBUS` on an unreadable cache entry

Not a `models/common` bug, but it cost significant triage time and is cheap to improve.

`tt_cache/tttv2/attention_1d` had been seeded in February 2026 and never refreshed. Reading one of those entries killed the process outright:

```
Fatal Python error: Bus error
  File ".../ttnn/operations/core.py", line 588 in load_tensor
  File "/work/models/common/modules/lazy_weight.py", line 121 in get_device_weight
```

The file was complete and correctly sized (295,272 bytes = 32 × 4608 × 2 + header) and the export had 7.3 TB free, so neither truncation nor space explains it — the mapping simply extends past what the file can serve. Because `SIGBUS` is uncatchable, there is no error message naming the file, and the failure is indistinguishable from a device fault.

Validating the header against the on-disk size before mapping would turn this into a diagnosable error. Related: a partially-written entry left behind by an aborted run produces the same signature, which makes any interrupted cache-population run silently poisonous to later ones.

---

## Suggested split

1. **B** — attention decode PCC. Wrong output, untracked, blocks the attention gate.
2. **A** — `local_indices`. Understood, four deletions, blocks the sampling gate. Needs a multi-device run to confirm.
3. **C** — tolerance failure, isolated.
4. **E** — `load_tensor` size validation, diagnosability only.
5. **D** — already tracked in #49081.

A and B are what make the TT-Transformers tier-1 unit entries red in #53911. That PR registers them per module, so each failure is attributable to one job rather than reddening the whole set, and it does not attempt to fix or mask either.
